report_name: Critical 'PHP2Shell' Flaws Put 70% of Websites at Risk of RCE

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Unauthenticated attackers exploit critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) in the public-facing PHP engine to gain remote code execution on web servers.

attack_patterns.name: Web Shell
attack_patterns.description: Attackers may place PHP web shells on compromised servers for persistence after exploiting the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: Post-exploitation, attackers use command and scripting interpreters like sh and bash, often spawned by the compromised web server process, to execute further commands.

malware.name: PHP2Shell
malware.description: Collective name for the exploit chain that leverages vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on servers running PHP.

tools.name: PHP
tools.description: The vulnerable scripting language engine targeted by the PHP2Shell exploits. Versions from 5.4 through 8.5 are affected.

tools.name: sh
tools.description: A suspicious child process spawned by a compromised web server process (e.g., apache2, nginx, php-fpm), indicating command execution.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: A suspicious child process spawned by a compromised web server process (e.g., apache2, nginx, php-fpm), indicating command execution.

tools.name: curl
tools.description: A suspicious child process spawned by a compromised web server process, likely used for downloading additional tools or payloads.

tools.name: wget
tools.description: A suspicious child process spawned by a compromised web server process, likely used for downloading additional tools or payloads.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-109618
vulnerabilities.description: A memory corruption vulnerability in PHP's core engine, which is the first part of the PHP2Shell exploit chain allowing for remote code execution.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-109619
vulnerabilities.description: A memory disclosure vulnerability in PHP's core engine, which is chained with CVE-2026-109618 as part of the PHP2Shell exploit to achieve remote code execution.

identities.name: UK Government Services
identities.description: A group of 32 UK government services that were taken offline as a precautionary measure while patching for the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.

indicators.name: Suspicious Web Server Child Process
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Web Server Child Process
id: 2b8a1c3d-f4e5-4b6a-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious child processes such as shells or downloaders being spawned by common web server processes, which can indicate post-exploitation activity following an RCE vulnerability like PHP2Shell.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-php-rce
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-22
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/apache2'
      - '/nginx'
      - '/php-fpm'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate web applications that are designed to call shell scripts or downloaders.
indicators.description: Detects suspicious child processes (sh, bash, curl, wget) spawned by web server processes (apache2, nginx, php-fpm), indicating potential RCE.

indicators.name: Potential Web Shell Creation in Web Root
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Web Shell Creation in Web Root
id: 5e6f7a8b-9c0d-4e1f-8a2b-3c4d5e6f7a8b
status: experimental
description: Monitors for the creation of new PHP files in common web root directories. This can indicate the deployment of a web shell for persistence after successful exploitation.
references:
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-php-rce
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-22
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.persistence
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - '/var/www/'
      - '/srv/www/'
      - '/usr/share/nginx/html/'
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.php'
  filter_legit_process:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/dpkg'
      - '/apt'
      - '/yum'
      - '/rpm'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_process
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate deployment of new PHP files by administrators or automated deployment tools.
indicators.description: Detects the creation of new .php files in common web directories, which could indicate the installation of a web shell for persistence.
